hilltop_citadel_towns.name: Hilltop Citadel Towns
hilltop_citadel_towns.observation: The old town wall is too long to hold, so the people crowd into a small walled citadel on the height.
hilltop_citadel_towns.social_consequence: The lower town is left to fall into ruin.

triple_line_land_walls.name: Triple Land Walls
triple_line_land_walls.observation: A moat, a low outer wall and a tall towered inner wall stand one behind another across the landward side.
triple_line_land_walls.ability_reason: A general defending the city can give ground wall by wall, and an attacker must win three lines under fire from the towers.

pass_command_garrisons.name: Pass Commanders
pass_command_garrisons.observation: A pass commander with a small garrison holds each mountain pass and questions everyone who crosses.

military_district_settlement.name: Military District Settlement
military_district_settlement.observation: Soldiers are given farms in the frontier districts, and their sons inherit both the land and the duty to serve.
military_district_settlement.ability_reason: A general can raise a ready local army in each district without paying it in coin.
military_district_settlement.social_consequence: The soldier-farmers grow into a proud caste, loyal first to their district's commander.

mounted_remount_school.observation: The state's studs breed and school cavalry horses, and each squadron draws its remounts from them.

bow_and_lance_cavalry.name: Bow-and-Lance Cavalry
bow_and_lance_cavalry.observation: The same rider shoots from the saddle at a distance and then charges home with the lance.

harbor_chain_booms.name: Harbor Chain Booms
harbor_chain_booms.observation: A chain floated on timbers is drawn across the harbor mouth at night and in time of war.

generals_field_manual.name: Generals' Field Manual
generals_field_manual.observation: A manual sets down for commanders how to order a march, pitch a camp, draw up the lines and deceive the enemy.
generals_field_manual.ability_reason: Generals learn from a book what generations learned in the field, so even a new commander can march and fight in good order.

paired_stirrups.name: Paired Stirrups
paired_stirrups.observation: A stirrup hangs on each side of the saddle, so the rider can stand and brace in the charge without being unseated.
paired_stirrups.ability_reason: Horsemen can strike and take blows at close quarters without being unhorsed, and cavalry becomes a shock arm in a general's hand.

high_bow_war_saddle.name: High-Bow War Saddle
high_bow_war_saddle.observation: A war saddle with high boards before and behind holds the rider in his seat when a lance strikes him.

raid_season_refuges.name: Raid-Season Refuges
raid_season_refuges.observation: In the raiding season the villagers drive their beasts and carry their grain into a walled enclosure on the hill.

arms_export_bans.name: Arms Export Bans
arms_export_bans.observation: No sword, mail or warhorse may be sold across the frontier, and the border guards search the carts.

lugged_war_spears.name: Lugged War Spears
lugged_war_spears.observation: Lugs below the spear blade stop it sinking too deep to pull free.

siphoned_liquid_fire.name: Siphoned Liquid Fire
siphoned_liquid_fire.observation: A bronze siphon in the warship's bow sprays burning oil that water cannot put out.
siphoned_liquid_fire.ability_reason: An admiral can burn an enemy fleet at close range, though the mixture's secret is kept by the ruler's own workshop.

spur_prow_galleys.name: Spur-Prow Galleys
spur_prow_galleys.observation: War galleys with a spur above the waterline to smash oars, and a lateen sail for the passage, form the fleet's backbone.

muster_rolls.name: Muster Rolls
muster_rolls.observation: The roll lists each holding's armed men, their horses and their gear, and the captain checks it at every muster.

river_raiding_ships.name: River Raiding Ships
river_raiding_ships.observation: Long shallow ships row far up the rivers, strike a town and are gone before the levy can gather.
river_raiding_ships.social_consequence: Riverside villages move their houses back from the banks.

mounted_retinue_summons.name: Summoned Mounted Retinues
mounted_retinue_summons.observation: Each lord answers the ruler's summons with his retinue of heavily armed horsemen, armed at his own cost.
mounted_retinue_summons.ability_reason: A general can gather a heavy mounted force within weeks, though its lords serve for a set term and quarrel over precedence.
mounted_retinue_summons.social_consequence: Power flows to the lords who keep armed horsemen, and the ruler depends on their loyalty.

castle_guard_rotations.name: Castle-Guard Rotations
castle_guard_rotations.observation: Paid knights take turns guarding the border castles, a set number of weeks each.

fortified_river_bridges.name: Fortified River Bridges
fortified_river_bridges.observation: A bridge with towers at each end closes the river to raiders' ships and holds the crossing.

realm_beacon_chain.name: Realm Beacon Chain
realm_beacon_chain.observation: Fires lit from hill to hill carry warning of a raid from the frontier to the court in a single night.

foreign_household_guard.name: Foreign Household Guard
foreign_household_guard.observation: The ruler's guard are foreigners sworn to him alone, with no kin in the realm to be bought.

captive_trained_corps.name: Captive-Trained Corps
captive_trained_corps.observation: Captive boys are bought, trained from youth and bound to the ruler as soldiers.
captive_trained_corps.social_consequence: The captive soldiers come to know their strength, and they begin to make and unmake rulers.

burgh_defense_network.name: Burgh Defense Network
burgh_defense_network.observation: Fortified towns stand a day's march apart, and each length of wall is manned by men from lands assigned to it.
burgh_defense_network.ability_reason: No raider is more than a day from a garrison, so a general can defend a whole realm from a network of strongholds.

rotating_half_levy.name: Rotating Half-Levy
rotating_half_levy.observation: Half the levy serves in the field while the other half farms, and they change places at set times.

shadowing_raid_defense.name: Shadowing the Raiders
shadowing_raid_defense.observation: Rather than meet raiders head on, the local levies follow them, pick off stragglers and strike when they turn home laden.

planned_ring_forts.name: Planned Ring Forts
planned_ring_forts.observation: Round forts built to one plan hold garrisons on a grid across the land.

twin_gate_passage.name: Twin-Gate Passage
twin_gate_passage.observation: The gate is a stone tower with a passage and a barred door at each end, so attackers who force one are trapped at the next.

motte_and_bailey.name: Motte and Bailey
motte_and_bailey.observation: A heaped earth mound crowned with a timber tower rises over a fenced yard, and it can be raised in a few weeks.
motte_and_bailey.ability_reason: A general can hold newly taken land by planting quick castles across it, each a base for a small garrison.
motte_and_bailey.social_consequence: The castles overawe the country around them, and the villagers who dug the mound resent the lord who sits on it.

kite_shield_cavalry.name: Kite-Shield Cavalry
kite_shield_cavalry.observation: Riders in mail carry long shields that cover the left side from shoulder to shin.

couched_lance_charge.name: Couched Lance Charge
couched_lance_charge.observation: Riders tuck the lance under the arm and charge knee to knee, so the horse's weight drives the point home.
couched_lance_charge.ability_reason: Close-ordered horsemen can break an enemy line in one charge, if the general picks his ground and his moment.

stone_keep_towers.name: Stone Keep Towers
stone_keep_towers.observation: A square stone tower several floors high holds the lord's hall, his stores and his last defense.
stone_keep_towers.ability_reason: A lord can hold out for months against anything short of a full siege, so a general must bring engines or starve the keep.

wall_top_hoardings.name: Wall-Top Hoardings
wall_top_hoardings.observation: Timber galleries built out over the wall top let defenders drop stones on men at the foot of the wall.

hearth_cover_curfew.name: Hearth-Cover Curfew
hearth_cover_curfew.observation: At the evening bell every hearth in the town must be covered with its lid, against fire in the night.

keep_cistern_stores.name: Keep Cisterns
keep_cistern_stores.observation: Deep wells and cisterns inside the keep give the garrison water for a siege of many months.

stirrup_cocked_crossbow.name: Stirrup-Cocked Crossbow
stirrup_cocked_crossbow.observation: An iron stirrup at the crossbow's nose lets the bowman stand on it and draw the string with both arms.

curtain_wall_flanking_towers.name: Flanking Towers
curtain_wall_flanking_towers.observation: Square towers jut out from the stone curtain wall, so archers can shoot along its face.

series_built_war_galleys.name: Arsenal-Built War Galleys
series_built_war_galleys.observation: The state arsenal builds war galleys one after another to one pattern, from timber cut and seasoned in advance.
series_built_war_galleys.ability_reason: An admiral can have a lost fleet replaced within a season, so the realm can lose a sea battle and still hold the sea.

mail_underpadding.name: Padding Under Mail
mail_underpadding.observation: A quilted coat under the mail spreads the force of a blow that the rings have stopped.

hue_and_cry.name: Hue and Cry
hue_and_cry.observation: When a crime is cried, every household must leave its work and join the chase of the felon.

hybrid_counterweight_engine.name: Hybrid Counterweight Engine
hybrid_counterweight_engine.observation: A box of stones hung on the throwing arm adds its weight to the crew hauling on the ropes.

service_money_commutation.name: Service Money
service_money_commutation.observation: Holders who would rather stay at home pay money in place of service, and the ruler hires soldiers with it.

sworn_frontier_brotherhoods.name: Sworn Frontier Brotherhoods
sworn_frontier_brotherhoods.observation: Brotherhoods of warriors sworn to a rule hold the frontier castles and answer to their own masters.

full_mail_harness.name: Full Mail Harness
full_mail_harness.observation: Mail covers the rider from head to foot: a hood, mittens and leggings.

siege_counter_forts.name: Siege Counter-Forts
siege_counter_forts.observation: The besiegers build forts of their own facing the town's gates, so no one goes in or out.

mounted_crossbowmen.name: Mounted Crossbowmen
mounted_crossbowmen.observation: Crossbowmen ride to the fight, dismount to shoot and remount to scout.

tournament_training.name: Tournament Training
tournament_training.observation: Knights fight mock battles, team against team, and learn to charge and rally together.

round_flanking_towers.name: Round Flanking Towers
round_flanking_towers.observation: Round and half-round towers turn aside the ram and have no corners for miners to undermine.

fireproof_roof_ordinance.name: Fireproof Roof Ordinance
fireproof_roof_ordinance.observation: After the great fire, every new house must be roofed with stone slates or tile instead of thatch.
fireproof_roof_ordinance.social_consequence: Poor householders who cannot afford tile are fined or driven outside the walls.

counterweight_engines.observation: A great beam swung by a falling box of earth and stone throws stones heavier than a man against the walls.
counterweight_engines.ability_reason: A besieging general can batter down a stone wall from beyond bowshot, and no curtain wall is safe any longer.

decimal_army_organization.name: Decimal Army
decimal_army_organization.observation: The army is ordered in tens, hundreds, thousands and ten-thousands, each under a commander answerable to the next.
decimal_army_organization.ability_reason: A general can command a host of a hundred thousand through a chain of officers, and every order has a path to follow.

multi_remount_riders.name: Riders with Remount Strings
multi_remount_riders.observation: Each rider leads several spare horses and changes mount as each tires, covering great distances at speed.

great_helm.name: Great Helm
great_helm.observation: A flat-topped iron helmet encloses the whole head, with slits for the eyes and holes for breath.

ocean_sailing.observation: Fleets and troop convoys cross the open sea out of sight of land, steered by compass and kept in company by signal.
ocean_sailing.ability_reason: An admiral can carry an army across open sea, land it on a far shore and keep it supplied there by convoy.

stone_machicolations.name: Stone Machicolations
stone_machicolations.observation: Stone galleries corbelled out over the gates let defenders drop stones through openings in the floor.

ship_fighting_castles.name: Ship Fighting Castles
ship_fighting_castles.observation: Wooden towers built at bow and stern of a merchant ship give archers a height to shoot from.

captured_engineer_corps.name: Captured Engineer Corps
captured_engineer_corps.observation: Engineers taken from conquered cities build the army's siege engines, and are well paid to do it.

compulsory_archery_practice.name: Compulsory Archery Practice
compulsory_archery_practice.observation: On rest days every commoner must shoot at the village butts, and each household must keep a bow.

ward_night_watch.name: Ward Night Watch
ward_night_watch.observation: Each ward of the town keeps its own night watch of citizens with lanterns and staves.

pressed_merchant_fleets.name: Pressed Merchant Fleets
pressed_merchant_fleets.observation: In war, merchant ships are seized, fitted with fighting castles and manned for the fleet.
pressed_merchant_fleets.social_consequence: Shipowners whose vessels are pressed lose a season's trade and seldom see fair payment.

concentric_castles.name: Concentric Castles
concentric_castles.observation: An inner ward of tall towers rises inside a lower outer ward, so defenders on both walls can shoot at once.
concentric_castles.ability_reason: A general holding a concentric castle can defend it with a small garrison against a great army for a whole season.

springald_wall_engines.name: Springald Wall Engines
springald_wall_engines.observation: Great crossbows mounted on the towers shoot heavy bolts at the besiegers' engines and their crews.

roadside_brush_clearance.name: Roadside Brush Clearance
roadside_brush_clearance.observation: Brush and trees are cleared a bowshot back from the high roads, so robbers have no cover.

coat_of_plates.name: Coat of Plates
coat_of_plates.observation: Iron plates riveted inside a cloth coat guard the body beneath the mail.
coat_of_plates.ability_reason: Men-at-arms can stand in the line against spear thrusts and arrows that once pierced mail.

armor_breaking_maces.name: Armor-Breaking Maces
armor_breaking_maces.observation: Flanged maces and war hammers crush through mail and plate where a sword would glance off.

belt_hook_spanning.name: Belt-Hook Spanning
belt_hook_spanning.observation: A hook on the crossbowman's belt lets him span the bow by straightening his back.

militia_pike_hedge.name: Militia Pike Hedge
militia_pike_hedge.observation: Town militia stand shoulder to shoulder in a hedge of long spears that horses will not charge into.
militia_pike_hedge.ability_reason: A general can hold ground against heavy horse with townsmen and farmers, if they keep their nerve.
militia_pike_hedge.social_consequence: Townsmen who have faced knights in the field and held begin to ask for a voice in council.

infantry_polearms.name: Infantry Polearms
infantry_polearms.observation: Long-hafted bills and axes let a foot soldier hook a rider from the saddle and cut him down.

nitre_incendiary_mixtures.name: Nitre Incendiaries
nitre_incendiary_mixtures.observation: Nitre stirred into pitch and sulfur makes fire pots and fire arrows that flare fiercely and are hard to smother.

massed_longbow_volleys.name: Massed Longbow Volleys
massed_longbow_volleys.observation: Ranks of archers loose their long bows together, and the arrows fall on the enemy like hail.
massed_longbow_volleys.ability_reason: A general can break charges and thin a host before it closes, with archers trained from childhood.

plate_limb_defences.name: Plate Limb Defences
plate_limb_defences.observation: Plates of iron shaped to arm and leg guard the limbs that mail left bruised and broken.

windlass_crossbow.name: Windlass Crossbow
windlass_crossbow.observation: A crank-wound windlass draws a heavy crossbow that no man could span with his arms alone.

visored_helmet.name: Visored Helmet
visored_helmet.observation: A pointed visor hinged to the helmet closes over the face and lifts when the fighting pauses.

black_powder.observation: Nitre, sulfur and charcoal ground together burn with a flash and a roar that the men who grind them learn to fear.
black_powder.ability_reason: The mixture is known only as a dangerous curiosity: no one can yet make it throw a stone, and it gives no general a new weapon.

free_mercenary_companies.name: Free Companies
free_mercenary_companies.observation: Bands of soldiers under contract captains sell their service to any paymaster, and plunder when they are unpaid.
free_mercenary_companies.social_consequence: Between wars the free companies live off the country, and villages pay them to pass by.

dispatch_code_lists.name: Dispatch Code Lists
dispatch_code_lists.observation: Lists of code words replace names and places in dispatches, so a captured letter tells the enemy little.
